items.title: Artificial Intelligence – COMIA 2026
items.description:

items.title: Transformation Enterprise Architecture with Agentic AI
items.description:
This book is a practical guide to transforming enterprise architecture in the age of generative AI. As intelligent systems reshape how organizations build, scale, and govern technology, this book bridges the gap between traditional architectural frameworks and the emerging GenAI-driven landscape. 
The book begins with an overview of enterprise architecture principles, including TOGAF, Zachman, and Gartner frameworks, and dives into core architectural layers—application, data, technology, infrastructure, and security. It then introduces the fundamentals of Generative AI, its model types, and its rapid evolution within enterprise contexts. The core of the book is how GenAI disrupts and elevates architectural thinking—from conversational modeling and automated decision records to reimagining design lifecycles through intelligent automation, augmentation, and autonomy. Readers will learn how to modernize application portfolios, document and repair APIs, and embed LLMs as intelligent middleware. Dedicated chapters explore GenAI's transformative impact on platform engineering, DevOps, cloud/edge infrastructure, observability, and AI-augmented governance. Key use cases include auto-generating code and configurations, orchestrating deployment pipelines with non-human agents, enabling self-documenting platforms, and enhancing security through GenAI-driven threat modeling and compliance enforcement. The book concludes by examining responsible AI practices and human oversight in autonomous architectures, offering practical insights into creating secure, scalable, and resilient systems powered by GenAI. 
Whether you're an architect or developer, this book provides a modern framework for applying GenAI across the enterprise stack and designing the next generation of intelligent, adaptive, and self-governing enterprise systems.

items.title: New Trends in Database and Information Systems
items.description:
This book constitutes short papers, demonstration papers, Doctoral Consortium School papers and workshop papers which were presented at the 30th European Conference on Advances in Databases and Information Systems, ADBIS 2026, which took place in Orléans, France, during September 28–October 1, 2026. They were carefully reviewed and selected for inclusion in this book. 

 A total of 18 short papers and 5 demonstration papers from the main conference are included in these proceedings, together with 4 Doctoral Consortium School papers and 13 workshop papers. 

 They were organized in the following topical sections: Similarity, topic modeling and knowledge graphs; Knowledge graphs, text-to-SQL and metadata extraction; Sustainability, privacy workflows and clinical analytics; Similarity search, truth discovery and anomaly detection; demos; Doctoral Consortium School; DEI4Teach: Diversity, Equity and Inclusion for Teaching Advanced Databases and Information Systems; MADEISD 2026: 8th Workshop on Modern Approaches in Data Engineering and Information System Design; FEHDA 2026: 2nd International Workshop on Fairness Exploration in Heterogeneous Data and Algorithms; and ERGA 2026: 2nd International Workshop on Entity Resolution and Graph Alignment.

items.title: Pattern Recognition. ICPR 2026 International Workshops
items.description: This 5-volume set LNCS 17110-7114 constitutes the proceedings of the ICPR 2026 International Workshops held under the umbrella of the 28th International Conference on Pattern Recognition, ICPR 2026, which took place in Lyon, France, during August 17–22, 2026. items.title: Electronic Voting
items.description:

items.title: Advances in Production Management Systems: Shaping the Future of Industry Through Sustainable, Data-Driven, and Human-Centric Production Systems
items.description:

The 269 full papers presented in these proceedings were carefully reviewed and selected from 320 submissions. They deal with up to date research in production management systems. This year's topic is “Shaping the Future of Industry through Sustainable, Data-Driven, and Human-Centric Production Systems”. 

The papers were categorized under the following topical sections: Sustainable, Circular and Responsible Production Systems; Collaborative Manufacturing, Service Systems and Lifecycle Management; Resilient, Sustainable and Digital Supply Networks; Smart Manufacturing, Digital Twins and Industrial Intelligence; Data-Driven and AI-Enabled Production Management; Human-Centred Production Systems, Work and Skills; Production Management Theory, Education and Research Methods.

items.title: Governance-First AI
items.description:
As Generative AI shifts from early excitement to real-world implementation, organizations face a critical crossroads. Executives demand rapid returns on investment, yet deployment is frequently stalled by risk, compliance, and governance barriers, and the rise of unmanaged Shadow AI systems has elevated the stakes. Governance-First AI confronts this tension head‑on, offering a practical, execution-ready guide for leaders seeking to move beyond hype and into secure, scalable adoption. 

 This book bridges the gap with a unified, governance‑first approach that enables enterprises to operationalise Generative AI confidently and responsibly. It confronts a landmark MIT NANDA finding — that 95% of enterprise generative AI initiatives deliver no measurable return — and traces the failure to its root: a systemic disconnect between solution architecture and enterprise governance. The authors present a cohesive framework for achieving Certified Operational Velocity, helping organisations evolve from experimental pilots to compliant, production-grade systems. At its core, the book translates stringent governance principles—including platform engineering and platform‑as‑a‑product thinking—into fifteen concrete architectural patterns. These blueprints address the full spectrum of enterprise AI challenges, from retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) deployment to context management, legacy system integration, and the auditable controls required for autonomous Agentic AI systems. Each chapter delivers step-by-step guidance for building secure, measurable, and future-proof AI capabilities. 

By introducing a unified governance-first architecture and pairing it with repeatable, production-ready use cases, Governance-First AI becomes the missing guide for unlocking AI’s true impact. It equips organizations to achieve transformative productivity gains—without compromising compliance—while preparing for the era of safe, autonomous AI.

items.title: Business Process Management: Responsible BPM Forum, Process Technology Forum, Educators Forum
items.description:
This book constitutes the proceedings of the BPM 2026 Responsible BPM Forum, Process Technology Forum, and Educators Forum held at the 24th International Conference on Business Process Management, BPM 2026, which took place in Toronto, Canada, during September/October 2026. 

The Responsible Business Process Management (RBPM) Forum provides a platform for exploring how to integrate responsibility into BPM practices, addressing challenges from three perspectives: technological, managerial, and conceptual. The Process Technology Forum covers technical and engineering aspects related to the study, design, development, and maintenance of software systems that support the modeling, simulation, analysis, enactment, and monitoring of business processes. The Educators Forum explores methods to improve BPM teaching in a dynamic and practice-oriented way. 

The 27 full papers included in this book were carefully reviewed and selected from a total of 65 papers submitted to the above-mentioned fora.
